**Synopsis:**
The Indian rupee closed at a near four-week high on August 31, gaining 0.2% for the month, supported by RBI intervention and MSCI index rebalancing inflows (~$1B expected). The currency had opened weaker due to rising oil prices tied to U.S.-Iran tensions and hawkish comments from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, which lifted September rate hike expectations. Analysts see a possible 25bps "protective" hike but note weakening jobs/manufacturing data could constrain the Fed. Technically, USD/INR is viewed as trending lower toward 93.50.
